stack.title: Cleopatra the seductress
stack.hook: The seductress is the most famous story about Cleopatra, but where did it come from?

cards.head: The seductress is the most famous story about Cleopatra, but where did it come from?

cr.line: Alma-tadema-antony-cleopatra.jpeg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: The original “siren”
cards.body: Ancient writers called Cleopatra a siren, a woman whose intelligence, beauty, and charm could captivate and distract powerful men. But did she actually weaponize her sexuality?

cr.file: Alexandre Cabanel - Cléopatre essayant des poisons sur des condamnés à mort.jpg
cr.line: Alexandre Cabanel - Cléopatre essayant des poisons sur des condamnés à mort.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: She fell in love with 2 of the most powerful men of her time
cards.body: When summoned in 41 BCE to meet Mark Antony, one of the three men then ruling Rome and the commander of its eastern provinces, she arrived on a golden ship, dressed as the goddess of Aphrodite, surrounded by music, perfume, and attendants.

cr.line: Cham - Charivari - V1d127-d.png. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: It was theater, and it worked flawlessly.
cards.body: She was more than just a pretty face. Cleopatra was brilliant, multilingual (Plutarch names seven peoples she spoke with without interpreters), politically savvy, and highly educated. She used conversation, wit, and knowledge as power. She knew how to read people and give them exactly what they wanted.

cards.head: THE TWO MEN, IN ORDER
cards.body: Julius Caesar came first, in 48 BCE. Mark Antony came seven years later, in 41 BCE. She had a son with Caesar and three children with Antony.

cr.line: Head of Julius Caesar from Tusculum MAntTorino 2089 n01.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: Her beauty was used against her
cards.body: Her opponent Octavian, who would later take the name Augustus, used the siren claims against her, claiming she bewitched Marc Antony into being her lover to take advantage of him, threatening Rome. He used it as a reason to go to war against her.

cards.head: WHY THIS THREATENED ROME
cards.body: In 34 BCE Antony gave Roman territory to her children and named Caesar's son the true heir. That attacked Octavian's own claim, so in 32 BCE Rome declared war on Cleopatra rather than on Antony.

cr.line: Berlín Cleopatra 01.JPG. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: The moment she captured Julius Caesar’s attention
cards.body: In 48 BC, 21-year-old Cleopatra had been driven from Alexandria by her brother Ptolemy XIII and desperately needed Julius Caesar’s support to regain her throne.

cr.artwork: Gladiators - wall painting in Pompei, in History of Rome and of the Roman people(1883) (14803382033).jpg
cr.file: Gladiators - wall painting in Pompei, in History of Rome and of the Roman people(1883) (14803382033).jpg
cr.line: Gladiators - wall painting in Pompei, in History of Rome and of the Roman people(1883) (14803382033).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: According to Plutarch, she secretly entered the palace bundled inside a bed-sack or bedding, carried in by her servant Apollodorus, the famous “rolled-up rug” is probably a later embellishment.

cr.line: Castro Battle of Actium.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: The stunt got her directly in front of Caesar, who was impressed by her boldness, backed her claim to the throne, and soon became her lover.

cards.head: WHY THE SMEAR OUTLIVED ROME
cards.body: Of Cleopatra's own writing, one word survives on a papyrus, and scholars still argue whether even that is her hand. With nothing to contradict them, her enemies got to define her permanently.
